rationale: The agent verified identity correctly using full name and zip, matched to a single user, and worked only within that account. It located the Texas order (#W5565470), summarized items accurately, and sought explicit confirmation before performing any order-changing action. When the user requested an Amex refund, the agent properly checked payment methods, explained limitations (only PayPal on file), offered an alternative, and proceeded only after the user agreed to refund to PayPal. The return was executed via the tool for the correct item IDs (kettle and keyboard), leaving the pet bed untouched, and the final status and refund method matched the tool’s output. One minor shortcoming is that the agent did not provide the tracking number for the Texas order; it initially provided a tracking number for a different order and then focused on the return once the user shifted the request. However, all policy-critical steps (authentication, confirmation before writes, correct execution, accurate final info) were met, so overall this meets the pass bar.
